phoneticConvention: Approximate English respelling for English-speaking readers (CAPITALS = stressed syllable; vowels ah / eh / ee / oh / oo; j and g before e/i → kh as in Scottish 'loch'; ñ → ny; ll → y; c before e/i and z → s; r is rolled; monosyllables in capitals). Standard Castilian with seseo and yeísmo. No substitute for the audio.
reviewStatus: Written by rule from validated content; native English review recommended.
title: My daily life
goal: Describe your daily life, habits and the people around you.

variants.study: Normalmente me levanto a las siete.
variants.phon: nohr-mahl-MEHN-teh MEH leh-VAHN-toh AH LAHS SEEEH-teh
variants.native: I usually get up at seven.

slot.native: have coffee with milk for breakfast

variants.study: Por la mañana desayuno café con leche.
variants.phon: POHR LAH mah-NYAH-nah deh-sah-YOO-noh kah-FEH KOHN LEH-cheh
variants.native: In the morning, I have coffee with milk for breakfast.

variants.study: Por la mañana voy al trabajo en metro.
variants.phon: POHR LAH mah-NYAH-nah VOHEE AHL trah-BAH-khoh EHN MEH-troh
variants.native: In the morning, I go to work by metro.

In the morning, I do some exercise.

variants.study: Por la noche veo la tele.
variants.phon: POHR LAH NOH-cheh VEH-oh LAH TEH-leh
variants.native: In the evening, I watch TV.

variants.study: Por la noche leo un poco.
variants.phon: POHR LAH NOH-cheh LEH-oh OON POH-koh

variants.study: Por la noche salgo con amigos.
variants.phon: POHR LAH NOH-cheh SAHL-goh KOHN ah-MEE-gohs
variants.native: In the evening, I go out with friends.

variants.study: Por la noche me acuesto pronto.
variants.phon: POHR LAH NOH-cheh MEH ah-KOOEHS-toh PROHN-toh
variants.native: In the evening, I go to bed early.
I live in a small flat.
I study Spanish in the afternoons.

variants.study: Todos los días voy al gimnasio.
variants.phon: TOH-dohs LOHS DEE-ahs VOHEE AHL kheem-NAH-seeoh
variants.native: Every day I go to the gym.
I often go to the gym.
I sometimes go to the gym.

variants.study: Los fines de semana voy al gimnasio.
variants.phon: LOHS FEE-nehs DEH seh-MAH-nah VOHEE AHL kheem-NAH-seeoh
variants.native: At weekends I go to the gym.

variants.study: Mi hijo mayor vive en Madrid.
variants.phon: MEE EE-khoh mah-YOHR VEE-veh EHN mah-DREED

My flat has lots of light.

variants.study: Mi piso tiene una cocina grande.
variants.phon: MEE PEE-soh TEEEH-neh OO-nah koh-SEE-nah GRAHN-deh

variants.study: En mi barrio hay un mercado.
variants.phon: EHN MEE BAH-rreeoh AHEE OON mehr-KAH-doh
variants.native: In my neighbourhood there's a market.

variants.study: En mi barrio hay muchos bares.
variants.phon: EHN MEE BAH-rreeoh AHEE MOO-chohs BAH-rehs
variants.native: In my neighbourhood there are lots of bars.

variants.study: En mi barrio hay un parque.
variants.phon: EHN MEE BAH-rreeoh AHEE OON PAHR-keh
variants.native: In my neighbourhood there's a park.

variants.study: En mi barrio hay una parada de metro.
variants.phon: EHN MEE BAH-rreeoh AHEE OO-nah pah-RAH-dah DEH MEH-troh
variants.native: In my neighbourhood there's a metro station.

variants.study: Los fines de semana voy a la playa.
variants.phon: LOHS FEE-nehs DEH seh-MAH-nah VOHEE AH LAH PLAH-yah

variants.study: Los fines de semana veo a mi familia.

model.note: Gender agreement: enfermero / enfermera, ingeniero / ingeniera, profesor / profesora.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Tienes hermanos?
turns.phon: TEEEH-nehs ehr-MAH-nohs
turns.native: Do you have brothers or sisters?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Sí, tengo un hermano y una hermana. ¿Y tú?
turns.phon: SEE, TEHN-goh OON ehr-MAH-noh EE OO-nah ehr-MAH-nah. EE TOO
turns.native: Yes, I have a brother and a sister. And you?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Yo tengo dos hijos.
turns.phon: YOH TEHN-goh DOHS EE-khohs
turns.native: I have two children.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: ¿Cuántos años tienen?
turns.phon: KOOAHN-tohs AH-nyohs TEEEH-nehn
turns.native: How old are they?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Diez y catorce. Mi hija mayor juega al baloncesto.
turns.phon: DEEEHS EE kah-TOHR-seh. MEE EE-khah mah-YOHR KHOOEH-gah AHL bah-lohn-SEHS-toh
turns.native: Ten and fourteen. My older daughter plays basketball.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: ¡Qué bien! ¿Vives cerca de aquí?
turns.phon: KEH BEEEHN. VEE-vehs SEHR-kah DEH ah-KEE
turns.native: Great! Do you live near here?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Sí, vivo en un piso cerca del centro.
turns.phon: SEE, VEE-voh EHN OON PEE-soh SEHR-kah DEHL SEHN-troh
turns.native: Yes, I live in a flat near the centre.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Yo también vivo en el centro, con mi familia.
turns.phon: YOH tahm-BEEEHN VEE-voh EHN EHL SEHN-troh, KOHN MEE fah-MEE-leeah
turns.native: I live in the centre too, with my family.

dialogues.practice: Listen to both roles, hide one role, answer, then swap one line for a variant of your own.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿En qué trabajas?
turns.phon: EHN KEH trah-BAH-khahs
turns.native: What do you do for a living?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Soy enfermera, trabajo en un hospital. ¿Y tú?
turns.phon: SOHEE ehn-fehr-MEH-rah, trah-BAH-khoh EHN OON ohs-pee-TAHL. EE TOO
turns.native: I'm a nurse, I work in a hospital. And you?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Trabajo desde casa, soy informático.
turns.phon: trah-BAH-khoh DEHS-deh KAH-sah, SOHEE een-fohr-MAH-tee-koh
turns.native: I work from home, I'm in IT.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: ¿A qué hora empiezas?
turns.phon: AH KEH OH-rah ehm-PEEEH-sahs
turns.native: What time do you start?

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: Normalmente me levanto a las siete y empiezo a las ocho y media.
turns.phon: nohr-mahl-MEHN-teh MEH leh-VAHN-toh AH LAHS SEEEH-teh EE ehm-PEEEH-soh AH LAHS OH-choh EE MEH-deeah
turns.native: I usually get up at seven and start at half past eight.

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Yo a veces trabajo de noche.
turns.phon: YOH AH VEH-sehs trah-BAH-khoh DEH NOH-cheh
turns.native: I sometimes work nights.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Y qué haces los fines de semana?
turns.phon: EE KEH AH-sehs LOHS FEE-nehs DEH seh-MAH-nah
turns.native: And what do you do at weekends?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Descanso y veo a mi familia.
turns.phon: dehs-KAHN-soh EE VEH-oh AH MEE fah-MEE-leeah
turns.native: I rest and see my family.

dialogues.practice: Listen to both roles, hide one role, answer, then swap one line for a variant of your own.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Dónde vives ahora?
turns.phon: DOHN-deh VEE-vehs ah-OH-rah
turns.native: Where do you live now?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Vivo en Valencia, en un piso pequeño.
turns.phon: VEE-voh EHN vah-LEHN-seeah, EHN OON PEE-soh peh-KEH-nyoh
turns.native: I live in Valencia, in a small flat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Cómo es el piso?
turns.phon: KOH-moh EHS EHL PEE-soh
turns.native: What's the flat like?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Tiene dos habitaciones y un balcón. Hay mucha luz.
turns.phon: TEEEH-neh DOHS ah-bee-tah-SEEOH-nehs EE OON bahl-KOHN. AHEE MOO-chah LOOS
turns.native: It has two bedrooms and a balcony. There's lots of light.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Y el barrio?
turns.phon: EE EHL BAH-rreeoh
turns.native: And the neighbourhood?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Muy bien. En mi barrio hay un mercado y una parada de metro.
turns.phon: MOOEE BEEEHN. EHN MEE BAH-rreeoh AHEE OON mehr-KAH-doh EE OO-nah pah-RAH-dah DEH MEH-troh
turns.native: Very good. In my neighbourhood there's a market and a metro station.

turns.speaker: A
turns.study: ¿Vas al trabajo en metro?
turns.phon: VAHS AHL trah-BAH-khoh EHN MEH-troh
turns.native: Do you go to work by metro?

turns.speaker: B
turns.study: Sí, todos los días.
turns.phon: SEE, TOH-dohs LOHS DEE-ahs
turns.native: Yes, every day.
